fix.passage: In Hoocak, an Indigenous language from the Mid-Atlantic region of what is now the United States, okayeke means “bad,” whereas ati okayeye’tesel means “bad houses.” This phenomenon, in which an element of a root word is repeated, sometimes with modification, within another word that is related to the root word, is called reduplication. <u>In this case, the element “ye” in okayeke gets repeated in ati okayeye’tesel.</u> There are many examples of this type of reduplication in Hoocak.

fix.passage: A run-of-river hydroelectric power plant, as the name suggests, uses the natural flow of a water source to generate electricity but is unable to start or stop that flow through its generators. Although peaking plants do not typically operate continuously as run-of-river plants do, peaking plants can generate more megawatt hours of power per year (MWh/yr) than some run-of-river plants.
